newsitem.title: GERMANY: SWIMMING-EUROPEAN RECORDS FOR SJOBERG AND VOLKER.
newsitem.headline: SWIMMING-EUROPEAN RECORDS FOR SJOBERG AND VOLKER.

text.p: Sweden's Johanna Sjoberg cracked a European record and earned herself 5,000 German marks ($3,240) at the European sprints and short-course swimming championships on Friday.
Sjoberg edged out German pre-race favourite Sandra Voelker as both beat the short-course 50 metres butterfly mark set by Inge de Bruijn of the Netherlands on December 8 1991.
But Voelker struck back with a European record of her own in the 100 metres freestyle later in the first session of finals.
Voelker, Olympic 100 freestyle silver medallist, surged home in the 100 freestyle in 53.04 seconds, beating the 53.33 of fellow German Franziska van Almsick in Beijing on January 10 1993.
She was only 0.03 seconds outside the world mark of China's Olympic champion Le Jingyi.
Sjoberg, 18, clocked 27.15 seconds and Voelker 27.23 in the 50 butterfly to better the 27.25 posted by de Bruijn at the 1991 European sprint championships in Gelsenkirchen, Germany.
Prize money for European records is on offer for the first time in a European championships.
Patrik Isaksson brought Sweden their second gold of the meeting with an upset win in the men's 50 metres breaststroke.
Isaksson, in an outside lane in the Neptun pool, pipped German Jens Kruppa by just 0.01 seconds, winning in 27.76.
Norway's Terrie Miller also contributed to a great afternoon for the Scandinavians by winning the women's 100 breaststroke.
Miller won in 1:07.91, overhauling Austria's Vera Lischka with a powerful finish.
Alicja Peczak of Poland was third, leaving 1995 world short-course silver medallist Svitlana Bondarenko of Ukraine, the fastest qualifier, without a medal in fourth place.
Italy's Emiliano Brembilla, fourth in the 400 and 1,500 freestyle at this year's Atlanta Olympics, claimed the first gold of these championships with a clearcut victory in the 400 freestyle.
He won by more than two seconds in 3:45.52 from Germany's Stefan Pohl, with Dimitrios Maganas of Greece, the fastest qualifier, third.
Chris Carol Bremer claimed the first victory for hosts Germany, touching just ahead of compatriot Thomas Rupprath in the 200 butterfly.
